newsitem.title: CHINA: China looks for active role from new U.N. chief.
newsitem.headline: China looks for active role from new U.N. chief.

text.p: China has told newly-appointed secretary general of the United Nations Kofi Annan it expects him to play an active role after he takes office on January 1, the official Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Annan's appointment showed that the career official from Ghana enjoyed the trust of the international community, Xinhua quoted Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen as writing in a letter to the new U.N. chief, who was sworn in on Tuesday.

"I believe that Your Excellency... will play an active role in safeguarding world peace and security, promoting economic and social development among countries and strengthening international cooperation," Qian wrote.

In a letter of congratulation to the government of Ghana, Chinese President Jiang Zemin expressed the belief that the United Nations would play a more active role in international affairs during Annan's five-year tenure, Xinhua said.
"The election of Mr. Annan to the post of Secretary-General is not only an honour for Ghana but also a pride for African countries and all developing countries," Jiang wrote.
During Annan's term, the good relations and cooperation between China and Ghana in international affairs and as U.N. members would be further developed and consolidated, he wrote.

China had supported Boutros Boutros-Ghali for re-election as secretary general, but was expected to be pleased with Annan's appointment because Jiang carried out a high-profile tour of Africa this year to try to boost China's standing on the continent.
